_about: Numbers transcribed by hand from the cited papers (PDFs downloaded with sha256 by pipeline.syn_sources; ids in 'source'). Used by the synthetic stage (pipeline/src/pipeline/stages/synthetic.py) to extend the catalogue below its completeness limit and to convert the Kuiper-belt model's g-band magnitudes to V. Everything else the synthetic stage uses comes from downloaded datasets (the SBDB snapshot, the NEO and Kuiper-belt model realizations, the smallbodies products).

completeness.model: H_lim(a) = -5 log10(a (a - 1 au)) + C (Eq. 5; a in au), C a free parameter per region
completeness.method: H_lim at each semimajor-axis bin = centre of the most populated H bin (Sec. 3.1: 'binning objects in both a and H and then identifying the H bin with the greatest number of objects'); H bin width 0.25 mag (Sec. 3.1); a-bin width 0.002 au for the fit, results unchanged for 0.01 and 0.05 au (Sec. 3.2); uncertainty of a bin's H_lim (Hmax - Hmin)/sqrt(n) (Sec. 3.2).
completeness.regionsTable1Note: Table 1 (MPCORB of 2019-09-29). Not used as numbers: C is refitted to the current catalogue on every build with the same method (the limit deepens as surveys go deeper, Sec. 4); the table is kept to compare.

mainBelt.table: Table 3, row 'All' (1814 main-belt asteroids, Subaru/HSC r band, debiased with per-CCD detection efficiencies)
mainBelt.form: Sigma(H) = dN/dH: 10^(alpha1 (H - H0)) for H < Hbreak, 10^(alpha2 H + (alpha1 - alpha2) Hbreak - alpha1 H0) for H >= Hbreak (Eq. 15)
mainBelt.sampleNote: Unbiased sample: heliocentric distance R <= 3.0 au and H_r <= 20.3 (Sec. 3.1).
mainBelt.vMinusRNote: Average m_V - m_r of main-belt asteroids from SDSS MOC4 used by the authors to convert to V (Sec. 4.3).

corroboration.text: Differential apparent-magnitude slope alpha = 0.218 +/- 0.026 for R = 20 to 23.5 mag, steepening to 0.340 +/- 0.025 for R = 23.5 to 25.6; constant fit 0.28 +/- 0.02 (abstract). Apparent-magnitude slopes equal absolute-magnitude slopes only for a single power law (Sec. 9.2); not used as a number, quoted as an independent check of alpha2.

jupiterTrojans.text: Cumulative slope alpha = 0.37 +/- 0.01 (N(H) proportional to 10^(alpha H)), single power law for 13.0 <~ H_r <~ 17.4 (abstract; Sec. 4, 'L4 JTs have a single-slope power-low size distribution in the range of 13.0 < Hr < 17.0'); for a single power law the differential slope is the same.
jupiterTrojans.vMinusRNote: V - r = 0.25 mag used by the authors (Szabo et al. 2007) to combine with the MPC catalogue (Sec. 4).

hildas.text: Differential slope alpha = 0.38 +/- 0.02 (abstract; Sec. 3.2, Eq. 3), single power law over ~1-10 km; unbiased sample r < 4.9 au and H < 18.0 (Fig. 3 caption).
hildas.vMinusRNote: m_V - m_r = 0.25 from the SDSS MOC4 Hildas (Sec. 3.2).

kuiperBeltColour.gMinusRText: 'a color of (g - r) = 0.70, corresponding to the mean (g - r) color of our full CFEPS sample' (Sec. 2, arXiv v1 p. 4, lines 72-73).

transformation.text: Table 1, all stars with R-I < 1.15: V = g - 0.59 (g - r) - 0.01 (rms 0.01).

kuiperBeltColour.note: V - g = -(0.59 (g - r) + 0.01) = -0.423 for the mean CFEPS colour. The CFEPS g is MegaCam g'; the star-based SDSS transformation is applied to it as is (a difference of order 0.1 mag, below the model's own H precision).
